# Bridgeland Builders — full reference

> Bridgeland Builders is a Winnipeg renovation contractor for kitchens, bathrooms, basements, whole-home renovations, home additions and commercial fit-ups in Winnipeg and nearby communities.

Renovation and construction contractor based in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. Not affiliated with Bridgeland, Texas or the Bridgeland neighbourhood of Calgary.

Phone: 431-866-5644 · Email: info@bridgelandbuilders.com · Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada · Free written quotes · Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. · Replies within one business day · Over 60 years combined experience · More than 100 projects completed

## Frequently asked questions

### General questions
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/faqs

**Q: How much does a renovation cost in Winnipeg?**
A: It depends on the size of the space, the scope, the finishes you choose and what we find behind the walls. For a starting range, try our free instant quote or read our cost guides for kitchens, bathrooms and basements. Your actual price comes in the free written quote after we have seen the space.

**Q: Are the on-site visit and the quote really free?**
A: Yes. The on-site visit and the written quote are both free, and there is no obligation to go ahead. We look at the space with you, talk through what you want, and then send a written quote with the scope, price and schedule, so you can decide in your own time.

**Q: What is the difference between the instant quote and a written quote?**
A: The instant quote is an online price calculator: you answer a few questions and see a starting price range in minutes. The written quote comes after our free on-site visit, once we have measured the space and agreed the scope. It sets out the work, the price and the schedule, with taxes shown.

**Q: What does the instant quote cover?**
A: Kitchen, bathroom and basement renovations. You pick the size of the space and your options, and it shows the starting range our estimator uses. It can’t see your home, so wiring, plumbing, structure and site conditions aren’t in it. Whole-home, addition and commercial projects aren’t covered: they are priced after a free on-site visit.

**Q: What makes a renovation cost more?**
A: The biggest factors are size, moving plumbing, walls or windows, the finishes you choose, and the condition of what is already there, such as old wiring, moisture or uneven floors. Permits, drawings and access also play a part. We point out the cost drivers at the on-site visit, so there are fewer surprises later.

**Q: What happens if the scope changes during the project?**
A: Changes happen, whether you decide to add something or a problem turns up behind a wall. Any change to the scope should be agreed, with its cost in writing, before that work is done, so ask how changes are handled when you review your written quote. In older homes, keep a contingency for surprises.

**Q: How do people pay for a renovation?**
A: Many homeowners talk to their own bank or credit union, and a home equity line of credit, which is secured by the home, is one option many consider. Businesses often look at bank loans or a landlord’s improvement allowance. Whichever route you take, get your written quote first, so you know how much you actually need to borrow.

**Q: Do I need a permit for my renovation in Winnipeg?**
A: Often, yes. Finishing a basement into living space or creating a new bedroom requires a building permit, and the City of Winnipeg says kitchens, bathrooms, open-concept changes and new or larger exterior openings may need one. Cosmetic work such as painting, flooring and millwork does not. Electrical or plumbing work can need its own permit. We confirm what your project needs at the on-site visit.

**Q: Do you handle permits and inspections?**
A: Yes. When a project needs permits or inspections, we include them in the plan and coordinate them with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality. The City notes that homeowners need the correct permits before certain renovations start, so we tell you what is needed and keep you informed as each inspection is booked and completed.

**Q: Who issues building permits outside Winnipeg?**
A: Outside the city, building permits come from the local municipality or planning district, and their requirements can differ from Winnipeg’s. Our service-area page lists who issues building permits in each community we serve, and we coordinate with that office for you as part of the project, just as we do with the City of Winnipeg.

**Q: How long does a renovation take?**
A: Most bathrooms take two to three weeks, most kitchens four to six weeks once the cabinets are on site, and basements four to eight weeks. Whole-home renovations and home additions usually run eight to sixteen weeks. Permits, product lead times and what we find when walls are opened can move these dates, and your written quote includes a schedule.

**Q: Can I stay in my home during the renovation?**
A: Often, yes. It depends on the size and location of the work. If it is your only bathroom or kitchen, we plan the order of work to keep the disruption as short as we can. At the on-site visit we explain what will be usable, how dust will be controlled and when to expect interruptions.

**Q: How will I know how my project is going?**
A: You get a progress update every week: what was done, what comes next, and any decisions we need from you. If something changes, such as a delivery date or a problem found behind a wall, we tell you and agree the next step with you before going ahead.

**Q: What areas do you serve?**
A: Bridgeland Builders serves Winnipeg and nearby communities within about an hour of the city, including Headingley, East St. Paul, West St. Paul, Oak Bluff, Selkirk and Steinbach. If you are a little further out, call us at 431-866-5644 and we will tell you honestly whether we can take on your project.

**Q: What types of projects do you take on?**
A: For homes, we renovate kitchens, bathrooms, basements and whole houses, and build home additions. For businesses, we renovate offices, retail stores, restaurants, cafés and bars, hotels, and medical, dental and physiotherapy clinics. We also install flooring, windows and doors, and handle exterior painting, masonry and stucco, and demolition.

**Q: Can you work after hours on a commercial renovation?**
A: Yes. For commercial projects we can schedule work after hours or on weekends, so your business can keep serving customers or patients while the renovation goes ahead. We plan the work around your lease dates and opening hours from the start, and send weekly updates so you always know what is happening next.

**Q: Do you take on smaller jobs as well as full renovations?**
A: Yes. Alongside full renovations, we quote smaller scopes such as new countertops or a backsplash, a new vanity or tub, flooring, windows and doors, or exterior painting. Tell us what you have in mind and we will scope just that part at the free on-site visit, with a written quote before anything starts.

**Q: Do you work with property managers, architects and designers?**
A: Yes. We quote vacant-unit turnovers, common areas, washrooms and multi-unit upgrades for property managers and building owners, and we build to supplied drawings and specifications from architects, engineers and interior designers. We walk the site against the drawings before work starts and raise anything that won’t work on site early, before it becomes a change order.

**Q: How do I get started?**
A: Use our free instant quote for a starting price range, call 431-866-5644, or book a free on-site visit online. We reply within one business day, arrange a time to see the space, and follow up with a written quote. Our office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

**Q: What are your office hours?**
A: Our office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed on weekends. Call 431-866-5644 during those hours, or email info@bridgelandbuilders.com or send your project details online at any time, and we will reply within one business day. Commercial renovation work itself can be scheduled after hours or on weekends.

**Q: What happens at the free on-site visit?**
A: We look at the space with you, take measurements, and talk through what you want to change, your budget range and your timing. We also check the things that affect the price, such as where the plumbing runs and the condition of what is there now. Then we prepare your written quote.

**Q: Does any work start before I approve the quote?**
A: No. Nothing starts until you have read and approved the written quote, which sets out the scope, price and schedule, with taxes shown. Once you approve it, we confirm the start date, help you with selections and coordinate any permits the project needs before work begins.

**Q: What should I have ready before the visit?**
A: A few photos or screenshots of what you like, a list of must-haves and nice-to-haves, and a rough budget range all help. Mention any known problems, such as leaks, past water in the basement or drafty windows, and any dates you are working toward, like a move-in or a lease start.

### Basement renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/basement-renovations

**Q: How long does basement development take?**
A: A typical basement takes four to eight weeks of work, depending on its size, the number of rooms, and whether a bathroom is added. Permit review and inspections are part of the schedule, so we build them into the timeline we give you with the written quote instead of leaving them as a surprise.

**Q: Do I need a permit to finish my basement in Winnipeg?**
A: Yes, if you are finishing a previously undeveloped basement or creating a new bedroom: the Winnipeg Building By-law requires a building permit for both. Updating finishes in a basement that is already developed does not need one. Electrical and plumbing work often need separate permits. We coordinate them as part of the job.

**Q: My basement smells damp. Can it still be finished?**
A: Usually, but not until the cause is known. Sometimes it’s grading or a downspout outside; sometimes it’s a foundation crack or a failing sump pump. Outside drainage gets fixed first, and active leaks or cracks go to a waterproofing or foundation repair company before we frame. Finishing over a damp wall only hides the problem.

**Q: What is an egress window, and do I need one?**
A: It’s a window large enough to climb out of in an emergency. The City’s basement guide says a new basement bedroom needs one that opens from inside without tools, with at least 0.35 m² of clear opening and no dimension under 380 mm, unless the bedroom has a door straight outside. We cut the opening, install the window, and set the window well.

**Q: Can you add a bathroom in the basement?**
A: Yes. If there’s no drain where you want the bathroom, we either break the concrete and run new drain lines or use an up-flush system. At the on-site visit we’ll tell you which suits your basement and what each involves, and the plumbing permit is part of the plan from the start.

**Q: Should I test for radon before finishing my basement?**
A: It’s worth doing. Health Canada recommends a long-term radon test of at least three months, ideally in fall or winter, on the lowest lived-in level. Test your current living space now, then again once the basement is in use. If a result is above 200 Bq/m³, a certified mitigation professional can recommend a fix.

**Q: We just bought a new house. Can we develop the basement right away?**
A: Usually, yes. A new house sold with an unfinished basement still needs a building permit to develop it, and the City requires a pre-board inspection of the insulated frost walls before they are covered. It also makes sense to run a long-term radon test through a fall or winter first, so results are in before walls go up.

**Q: Will the basement actually be warm?**
A: That comes down to insulation, air sealing and heat supply, and we plan all three. Walls are framed off the foundation and insulated with the vapour control on the warm side, and the new rooms get enough heat to stay comfortable in January. We also check how your furnace will handle the extra space.

### Basement suites
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/basement-suites

**Q: Can any basement become a legal suite?**
A: Not always. The lot must allow a secondary suite under the Zoning By-law, only one suite is allowed per single-family property, and the space must meet Manitoba Building Code items such as ceiling height, exits and egress windows. Where zoning isn’t met, conditional use approval or a variance may be needed. We start checking these at the on-site visit.

**Q: What makes a suite different from a finished basement with a kitchen?**
A: A suite is a separate home. The City treats an attached secondary suite as an independent dwelling unit with its own entrance, and it needs a development permit as well as a building permit. The building code then adds fire protection, a smoke-tight barrier, sound control, alarms and exits that an ordinary finished basement doesn’t need.

**Q: How long does a basement suite take to build?**
A: Our typical basement development takes four to eight weeks of construction. A suite adds a kitchen, fire and sound separation, and more inspections, and both the development and building permits have to be in place before building starts. We give you a schedule for your suite with the written quote, and update it every week once work begins.

**Q: Is there government help to build a secondary suite?**
A: Since January 15, 2025, federal mortgage insurance rules have let eligible homeowners refinance to build a secondary suite, with financing of up to 90 per cent of the home’s value including the value the suite adds. The Canada Secondary Suite Loan Program announced in 2024 will not be implemented, according to Budget 2025. Ask your lender what you qualify for.

**Q: Is there a tax credit for a family suite?**
A: Possibly. Canada’s Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit covers certain expenses to create a self-contained secondary unit that lets a senior, or an adult eligible for the disability tax credit, live with a qualifying relative. Eligibility and amounts depend on your situation, so confirm with the Canada Revenue Agency or your accountant before counting on it.

**Q: Should the basement be checked for moisture and radon first?**
A: Yes. A suite is someone’s home, so the basement must be dry before framing, and active leaks or foundation cracks go to a waterproofing or foundation specialist first. Health Canada recommends a long-term radon test of at least three months, ideally in fall or winter, and a certified mitigation professional if levels exceed 200 Bq/m³.

**Q: What happens at the free on-site visit?**
A: We measure ceiling heights, look at the window openings and where a separate entrance could go, and check where the furnace, water heater, panel and drains sit. We talk through who the suite is for. You then receive a written quote, and we confirm the zoning and permit route for your lot before the layout is set.

### Bathroom renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/bathroom-renovations

**Q: How long does a bathroom renovation take?**
A: Two to three weeks for a typical full bathroom, from demolition to the final clean. If it’s your only bathroom, tell us at the on-site visit: we plan those jobs so the toilet is back in service as early as possible, and we let you know in advance which days the water will be off.

**Q: Can you move the toilet or shower to a different spot?**
A: Usually, yes. It depends on where the drains and floor joists run, and on a concrete slab it means breaking and re-pouring part of the floor. At the on-site visit we’ll tell you whether the move is a small change or a bigger one, and the written quote shows what it involves.

**Q: Do you supply the tile and fixtures, or do I?**
A: Either works. Most people choose from options we bring; some prefer to shop for their own. If you supply materials, have them on site before the start date so the schedule holds, and check the sizes with us first so the vanity, toilet and shower fit the plan.

**Q: Can you install heated floors?**
A: Yes. A bathroom renovation is the right time to add them, since the floor is already open. The heating mat goes under the tile on its own circuit with a thermostat, and the wiring may need its own electrical permit. On a cold Winnipeg morning, a warm floor makes a real difference.

**Q: What if you find water damage under the old shower?**
A: It happens, especially under older tubs and showers. We photograph it, show you, and price the repair in writing before going further. Rotten subfloor is replaced, never tiled over, because new tile on a damaged floor won’t last. Catching it during demolition is far better than finding it after.

**Q: Who arranges the permits and inspections?**
A: We coordinate them. When your bathroom needs a building permit or plumbing and electrical permits, we arrange them with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality and schedule inspections before the walls are closed. The City says the homeowner and the permit applicant share responsibility for inspections, so you’ll know what was booked and passed.

**Q: What happens at the free on-site visit?**
A: We measure the room, look at the plumbing, venting and floor, and talk about what you want to change. You then receive a free written quote listing labour, materials and what’s included, so it is easy to compare with any other company’s quote. If you later swap a tile or a vanity, we re-price it before anything is ordered.

### Home additions
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/home-additions

**Q: How long does a home addition take?**
A: Many straightforward additions take eight to sixteen weeks once permits and materials are ready. Size, soil and foundation conditions, structural changes, and custom finishes all affect the schedule. You get a timeline with your written quote, and a progress update every week once construction starts, so changes never come as a surprise.

**Q: Who prepares the drawings for an addition?**
A: Every addition needs drawings for the development and building permit applications, and the City requires an engineer’s sealed drawing for structural work beyond Part 9 of the Manitoba Building Code. At the on-site visit we talk through who will prepare them for your project, and we build to the approved drawings.

**Q: Can you make the addition match my existing house?**
A: That is the goal from the start. We look at rooflines, windows, siding or masonry, floor heights, trim and interior finishes so the addition connects as naturally as possible. Where an exact match isn’t available, we’ll show you the closest options and where a deliberate contrast might look better.

**Q: Can we stay in the house while the addition is built?**
A: Usually, for most of the project. The existing house stays closed off while the foundation and shell go up. The wall between old and new is opened only once the addition is weather-tight, and we plan that step and the interior connection to keep the disruption as short as possible.

**Q: Can the addition include a kitchen or bathroom?**
A: Yes. Plumbing, electrical, ventilation, heating and structure are planned from the start so those rooms are properly tied into the home’s systems. Kitchens and bathrooms in an addition also need the trade permits that go with them, which we coordinate along with the development and building permits.

**Q: Should I build an addition or develop my basement?**
A: If your basement is unfinished and has enough ceiling height, developing it usually adds living space with less structural work. An addition makes more sense when you need the room on the main floor, want more daylight, or the basement is already in use. We can look at both options at the on-site visit.

**Q: What happens at the free on-site visit?**
A: We look at the yard, the existing foundation, roofline and exterior, and where the addition would join the house. We talk about the space you need and the zoning questions to check. You then receive a written quote with the scope, so you can see what is included before any permit applications go in.

### Kitchen renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/kitchen-renovations

**Q: How long does a kitchen renovation take?**
A: Most full kitchens take four to six weeks once the cabinets are on site. Countertops are templated after the cabinets are set, which adds about a week in the middle. Cabinets are ordered as soon as you approve the written quote, so the build isn’t left waiting on them.

**Q: Will we have a working kitchen during the renovation?**
A: You’ll be without the sink and stove for most of the build. We set up a temporary counter with your kettle, microwave and fridge so you have somewhere to make coffee and simple meals. If anyone in the house has particular needs, tell us at the on-site visit and we’ll plan around them.

**Q: Can you remove the wall between the kitchen and living room?**
A: Usually. A non-structural wall is straightforward. A load-bearing wall needs a beam sized for the load and a building permit, and the City requires an engineer’s sealed drawing when the structure goes beyond what Part 9 of the Manitoba Building Code covers. We’ll tell you at the on-site visit which kind of wall you have.

**Q: Should I choose stock, semi-custom or custom cabinets?**
A: Stock cabinets are quicker and cost less, and they suit most standard layouts. Semi-custom adds more sizes, finishes and interior options. Fully custom makes sense when the room is an odd shape or you want storage built around specific things. We can price more than one option in the written quote so you can compare.

**Q: Can I keep my existing appliances?**
A: Yes. Tell us early so the cabinet openings are built to fit them. If you plan to replace appliances later, send us the model numbers of the ones you have in mind and we’ll size the openings for those now, so nobody is cutting into new cabinets in two years.

**Q: Who arranges the permits and inspections?**
A: We do. When your kitchen needs a building permit or trade permits, we coordinate them with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality and schedule each inspection as the work reaches that stage. The City says the homeowner and the permit applicant share responsibility for inspections, so we keep you informed at every step.

**Q: What happens at the free on-site visit?**
A: We measure the kitchen, look at the plumbing, wiring and walls, and talk through how you cook and what frustrates you about the current layout. After the visit you receive a written quote that lists what’s included, so you can read it line by line, and compare it with another company’s quote, before deciding anything.

### Whole home renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/whole-home-renovations

**Q: How long does a whole home renovation take?**
A: Most run eight to sixteen weeks, depending on the size of the house and how much of it is being renovated. You get a schedule with your written quote, and if something shifts we tell you the same week in your progress update, not at the end of the job.

**Q: Can we stay in the house while you work?**
A: Often, yes, if we stage the work in sections and keep a kitchen and a bathroom usable for you. Sometimes it’s faster and simpler to move out for a few weeks. We lay out both options at the on-site visit, with what each means for the schedule, and let you decide.

**Q: Who handles the permits and inspections?**
A: We coordinate them. Where the work needs building, electrical or plumbing permits from the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality, we arrange the applications and schedule the inspections at each stage. If structural changes need an engineer’s sealed drawing, we build that step into the schedule before demolition starts.

**Q: Do I pick the materials, or do you?**
A: You do; we help narrow it down. We bring options that fit your budget and hold up over time, and you choose from there. If you’d rather hand most of the decisions to us, that works too. Either way, every selection is written into the scope before anything is ordered.

**Q: What happens if you find something unexpected behind a wall?**
A: It happens in older homes: outdated wiring, water damage, sometimes a wall carrying more load than it should. Ask at the on-site visit how anything found behind the walls would be handled and priced, and keep a contingency for it. Suspect materials such as old vermiculite insulation are left undisturbed until a professional has tested them.

**Q: Should we renovate all at once or in stages?**
A: All at once is usually faster and keeps the disruption to one period, but you may need to move out for part of it. In stages, you live in the house while sections are finished one by one, which takes longer overall. We set out both options and their timelines at the on-site visit.

**Q: How will we know what’s happening each week?**
A: You get a progress update every week: what was finished, what’s next, any decisions we need from you, and anything that has changed. If something affects the schedule, you hear about it that week. Questions between updates are welcome by phone at 431-866-5644 or email during business hours.

### Commercial renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/commercial-renovations

**Q: Can you work after hours so we stay open?**
A: Yes. Evening and weekend scheduling is available for commercial work, and for stores and restaurants it’s often the plan from the start. In Winnipeg, loud work within 150 m of a home is limited to 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. on weekends, so noisy tasks are scheduled inside those hours.

**Q: Do you handle permits and inspections?**
A: Yes. We coordinate building permits and inspections with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality, and we flag anything in your space that will need attention early, such as a change of use, a fire separation or an accessibility upgrade. If the City requires an architect’s or engineer’s drawings, we build to theirs.

**Q: What is a tenant improvement?**
A: A tenant improvement, also called a fit-up, fit-out or leasehold improvement, is the work that turns a leased commercial unit into a space one business can use: walls, ceilings, lighting, washrooms, finishes and services. Your lease usually says who pays for what, so bring it to the site visit and we’ll scope the work against it.

**Q: Can you work with our architect or designer?**
A: Yes. We build to supplied drawings and specifications, and we walk the space against them before work starts. If something on the drawings won’t work on site, such as a duct that clashes with a beam, we raise it with you and your designer before it turns into a costly change.

**Q: Can you take on work for property managers?**
A: Yes. We quote vacant-unit turnovers, common areas, washrooms and multi-unit upgrades for property managers and building owners. Each job starts with a free site visit and a written quote, and the weekly progress update gives you something to pass on to owners and tenants.

**Q: How firm is the schedule?**
A: The schedule comes with your written quote, and we build to it. If something outside our control moves, like a permit review, a supplier delay or an inspection date, you hear about it in that week’s update along with what we’re doing about it, rather than at the end of the job.

**Q: Which areas do you serve for commercial work?**
A: We work in Winnipeg and nearby communities within about an hour of the city, including Headingley, East St. Paul, West St. Paul, Oak Bluff, Selkirk and Steinbach. Outside Winnipeg, permits and inspections go through the local municipality or planning district, and we coordinate with them the same way.

**Q: How quickly will you get back to us?**
A: Within one business day. Our office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and you can reach us at 431-866-5644 or info@bridgelandbuilders.com. From there we book a free on-site visit, walk the space with you, and follow up with a written quote.

### Office renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/office-renovations

**Q: How long does an office renovation take?**
A: It depends on the scope and on the permit. A refresh of finishes in the same layout moves quickly, while a full fit-up with new walls, ceilings and services takes longer and waits on the City’s plan review. You get a schedule with your written quote, built backwards from your move-in date, and an update every week.

**Q: Can my staff keep working during the renovation?**
A: Often, yes. We split the space into phases so part of the office stays usable, keep the work area closed off, and schedule the loudest work for evenings and weekends where the City’s noise rules allow. Some steps, like new flooring under desks, may need a weekend or a short move, and we’ll name those at the site visit.

**Q: Will my office renovation need an architect?**
A: Not always. The City of Winnipeg’s guide says structural changes need a professional engineer, and significant changes to fire alarms, sprinklers, exits or public corridors need an architect and/or engineer. A simple layout change inside one unit may not. Bring your plans to the site visit and we’ll tell you what the City is likely to ask for.

**Q: Who pays for an office fit-up, the landlord or the tenant?**
A: Your lease decides. Some landlords offer a tenant improvement allowance or build part of the space before you move in; others hand over a bare unit. Read the improvement clause or work letter before you collect quotes, and bring it to the site visit so the scope matches what you’re responsible for.

**Q: Can you add meeting rooms or private offices?**
A: Yes. New partitions, doors and ceilings for meeting rooms and private offices are a common part of an office renovation. Each new room also needs light, power, data, air flow and enough sound control for how it’s used, so we plan those with the walls rather than after them.

**Q: Do you handle the permit and inspections?**
A: Yes. We coordinate the building permit and inspections with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality, and flag anything that will need attention early, such as a demising wall, an exit change or an accessibility upgrade. If the City needs professional drawings, we build to the architect’s or engineer’s set.

**Q: What happens after I contact you?**
A: We reply within one business day and book a free on-site visit. We walk the space with you, go through the lease dates and what your team needs, and then send a written quote with a schedule. Once the work starts, you get a progress update every week until handover.

### Retail renovations
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/retail-renovations

**Q: Can you renovate while the store stays open?**
A: Often. We phase the sales floor, keep the work area closed off from customers, and schedule loud work outside your trading hours, within the City’s noise limits near homes. Some steps, like flooring at the entrance or a storefront change, may need a short closure; we’ll show those in the schedule so you can plan around them.

**Q: How long does a retail fit-out take?**
A: It depends on the scope and the permit. A refresh of finishes in the same layout moves faster than a full fit-out with new walls, washrooms and services, which also waits on the City’s plan review. You get a schedule with your written quote, built backwards from your opening date, and an update every week.

**Q: Do I need a permit for a new store sign?**
A: Yes. The City of Winnipeg says to get a permit before starting any construction or alteration to any part of a sign, and new internally lit signs need a separate electrical sign permit. If a sign company is supplying your sign, confirm at the site visit who is applying for the permit so the storefront work and sign installation line up.

**Q: Can you work to our brand or head-office drawings?**
A: Yes. We build to supplied drawings and specifications, whether they come from your designer, your landlord’s design criteria or a head-office fit-out package. We walk the unit against them before work starts and raise anything that won’t work on site before it becomes a change order or a delay.

**Q: Does a retail renovation need an occupancy permit?**
A: Often. In Winnipeg, a new tenant establishing a use without a valid occupancy permit, or a tenant expanding into more space, generally needs one before opening. A new tenant moving into a space that already has a valid occupancy permit, with no alterations or change of use, generally does not. Ask your landlord what permit the unit has.

**Q: Do you renovate showrooms?**
A: Yes. A commercial showroom renovation follows the same process as a store: a free site visit, a written quote and a schedule around your hours. Showrooms usually need more attention on lighting, power at display locations and flooring that can take heavy products, so bring your display plan to the site visit.

**Q: What happens after I get in touch?**
A: We reply within one business day, Monday to Friday, and book a free on-site visit. We walk the unit with you, go through your dates and drawings, and then send a written quote with a schedule. Once work starts, you get a progress update every week until the store is handed over.

### Restaurants & hospitality
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/restaurant-renovations

**Q: Can you renovate while we stay open?**
A: Often, yes. We work after close, on your closed days and on weekends, and phase the job so part of the room keeps serving. In Winnipeg, loud work within 150 m of a home must stop at 9 p.m., so noisy tasks go into daytime closures. Kitchen work that touches plumbing or ventilation may need a short full closure, and we’ll say when.

**Q: Do restaurant plans need health approval in Manitoba?**
A: Yes. Manitoba’s guideline requires the owner to submit a registration form and a scaled plan showing equipment, plumbing fixtures and finishes to the local public health inspector for approval before construction, renovation or conversion begins. The health permit is issued only after an inspection once construction is complete, so the schedule allows for both steps.

**Q: Do you renovate commercial kitchens?**
A: Yes. Commercial kitchen renovation covers walls, ceilings and floors in cleanable materials, hand, prep and dish sinks, floor drains, and the rough-ins for hoods and equipment. The hood and fire suppression design comes from your designer, engineer and hood supplier; we build to it and sequence the trades so inspections happen in the right order.

**Q: Does my restaurant need a grease interceptor?**
A: Plan on one. Manitoba’s food premises guideline says properly sized grease traps or interceptors serving the utensil washing sinks must meet the Manitoba Plumbing Code and be easy to reach for cleaning; check the City’s sewer requirements too. Settle the size and location at the plan stage, since an interceptor is hard to move later.

**Q: Do you renovate hotels?**
A: Yes. We renovate guest rooms and bathrooms, corridors, lobbies, breakfast rooms and meeting rooms. Work is phased by room, floor or wing so the rest of the hotel keeps operating, noisy tasks are kept to daytime hours, and you get a weekly update to share with management or ownership.

**Q: We serve alcohol. Does a renovation affect our liquor licence?**
A: It can. The Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba says it is the licensee’s responsibility to notify the LGCA if major renovations are made to licensed premises. Check with them before work starts, especially if the bar, seating or floor plan is changing, and build their timeline into your opening date.

**Q: Can you build to our designer’s drawings?**
A: Yes. We build to supplied drawings and specifications for dining rooms, bars and kitchens, and walk the space against them before work starts. If a detail won’t work on site, such as a drain that can’t reach the planned sink location, we raise it with you and your designer before it becomes a costly change.

**Q: Do you work outside Winnipeg?**
A: Yes, within about an hour of the city, including Headingley, East St. Paul, West St. Paul, Oak Bluff, Selkirk and Steinbach. The building permit then comes from the local municipality or planning district, and the health plan review still goes to your area public health inspector before construction starts.

### Medical & dental offices
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/medical-dental-office-renovations

**Q: Can our clinic stay open during the renovation?**
A: Often, yes. We phase the work so some operatories or exam rooms keep seeing patients while others are rebuilt, keep the work area closed off, and move the loudest tasks to evenings and weekends where the City’s noise rules allow. Some steps, like tying in new plumbing, may need a short closure, and we’ll name those in the schedule.

**Q: Do you build dental operatories and sterilization rooms?**
A: Yes. Dental office construction covers the walls, cabinetry and finishes as well as the plumbing, power and data rough-ins each chair needs. We build to your equipment supplier’s installation drawings and your designer’s layout, so ask your supplier for those early: they decide where every rough-in goes.

**Q: Do clinic renovations need special finishes?**
A: Usually. Clinical areas are cleaned often and with strong products, so smooth, non-porous, durable surfaces with few seams are the usual choice: sheet flooring with coved edges, solid-surface or quartz counters, and scrubbable wall finishes. Your clinical policies and your designer set the exact specification, and we build to it.

**Q: What do we need to know about X-ray rooms?**
A: Plan them first. Under Manitoba’s X-Ray Safety Regulation, X-ray equipment must be registered, and installing a machine in a permanent location needs the minister’s prior approval, with scaled drawings showing the shielding on the room’s boundaries. Once you have the shielding design, we build the walls, doors and ceiling to match it.

**Q: Will the renovated clinic be accessible?**
A: It’s built to the Manitoba Building Code, which adopted the 2020 National Building Code on January 1, 2024, with updated accessibility requirements aligned with CSA B651. That shapes entrances, washrooms, door widths and reception counters. Older clinics may have features worth upgrading during the work, and we’ll point those out at the site visit.

**Q: Do you work with our designer and equipment supplier?**
A: Yes. We build to supplied drawings and specifications, and we coordinate site access with your equipment supplier so cabinets, rough-ins and equipment arrive in the right order. If a drawing doesn’t work on site, we raise it before the wall is closed, not after.

**Q: Do you handle permits and inspections?**
A: Yes. We coordinate the building permit and inspections with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality, and flag early anything your space will need, such as an accessibility upgrade, an exit change or professional drawings. Approvals that belong to you, like X-ray equipment registration, stay with you, and we build the schedule around them.

### General contracting
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/general-contracting

**Q: How do general contractors charge?**
A: Usually in one of three ways: a fixed price for a defined scope, cost-plus (the cost of labour and materials plus a fee or percentage), or a construction-management fee. Whatever the method, make sure the scope, any allowances and how changes are priced are written down. Our written quote sets out the scope and price for your project.

**Q: Do I need a general contractor, or can I hire the trades myself?**
A: You can hire trades yourself, but then you take on the scheduling, permits, inspections and the gaps between trades, such as who patches the drywall the electrician opened up. A general contractor takes that coordination on and prices the whole job in one written quote. It usually makes sense once more than two or three trades are involved.

**Q: Can you build from our architect’s or designer’s drawings?**
A: Yes. We build to supplied drawings and specifications for residential and commercial projects. Before work starts we walk the site against the drawings, ask questions, and raise anything that won’t work as drawn, so it’s resolved with your architect or designer before it becomes a change order or holds up an inspection.

**Q: Do you handle permits and inspections?**
A: Yes. We coordinate building permits and inspections with the City of Winnipeg or your local municipality and book inspections before work is closed up. On commercial projects in Winnipeg, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and demolition permits are applied for by City-licensed contractors, so those trades are lined up as part of the plan.

**Q: What is the holdback on a construction contract in Manitoba?**
A: Under Manitoba’s Builders’ Liens Act, the person paying for the work must hold back 7.5% of each payment and keep it for at least 60 days after substantial performance is certified, the work is completed or it is abandoned. Ask your lawyer how it applies to your contract, and raise it with us when we go through your quote.

**Q: Do you take on residential and commercial projects?**
A: Both. On the residential side we manage kitchens, bathrooms, basements, whole-home renovations and additions; on the commercial side, offices, stores, restaurants, hotels and clinics. Commercial work can be scheduled after hours and on weekends, and every project, of either kind, starts with a free on-site visit and a written quote.

**Q: How do you keep clients updated?**
A: With a progress update every week: what was done, what’s next, and anything that has changed, such as a delivery date or an inspection result. If something moves that affects your schedule, you hear about it that week, not at the end. You can also reach us at 431-866-5644 or info@bridgelandbuilders.com.

### Windows and doors installation
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/windows-and-doors

**Q: Can you make a window opening bigger?**
A: Yes. A new or larger opening in an exterior wall can need a building permit in Winnipeg, and it needs a header sized for the wall above. A basement bedroom window must also meet egress size rules. We plan all of that, and sort out the permit, before the wall is cut.

**Q: Do you replace windows in winter?**
A: Yes, with planning. Each opening is closed up as soon as the new unit is set, so heat loss stays limited. Sealants and some foams list minimum application temperatures, so on very cold days some exterior sealing may wait for a milder day.

**Q: Should I get a quote for triple-pane windows?**
A: It’s worth pricing. Triple-pane units generally insulate better than double-pane, and Efficiency Manitoba’s rebate currently applies only to ENERGY STAR certified triple-pane products. Double-pane can still suit a tight budget or a space the rebate excludes, such as a garage. We can quote both so you can compare.

**Q: What do I need for the Efficiency Manitoba rebate?**
A: Each window or door needs an NRCan reference number, so ask for those numbers on your quote and invoice. Only replacements in your primary residence qualify, not new openings, and the application is due within 90 days of installation and payment in full. Check efficiencyMB.ca for current terms.

**Q: Do you replace windows in older or character homes?**
A: Yes. Older houses often have out-of-square openings and trim worth keeping, so we measure carefully and plan the trim before ordering. If the house is in a heritage conservation district or on the City’s heritage list, a heritage permit may be needed first, and we check that before anything is ordered.

**Q: How much does window or door replacement cost?**
A: It depends on the number of units, their sizes, frame material and glass, and how much repair each opening needs. We don’t guess from a photo: the on-site visit and written quote are both free, and the quote lists every unit so you can compare it line by line.

### Exterior painting
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/exterior-painting

**Q: Why is my exterior paint peeling?**
A: Peeling usually comes from moisture getting behind the paint, poor adhesion to a dirty or chalky surface, or too many old layers. We look for the cause at the on-site visit, such as a leaking gutter or missing caulking, because painting over it brings the peeling back.

**Q: Can you paint stucco?**
A: Yes, when it is sound. Cracks are repaired first, and a masonry paint is used so moisture can still escape. Stucco that has never been painted is a bigger decision, because once painted it needs repainting from then on. If paint isn’t the right fix, we will tell you.

**Q: Can exterior painting be done in the fall?**
A: Often, as long as the days and nights stay inside the paint’s temperature range and the walls are dry. Shorter days and colder nights slow drying, so each side is planned around the forecast. If the season runs out, booking the work for spring beats painting into frost.

**Q: Is the old paint on my house lead-based?**
A: If the house was built before 1960, Health Canada says it probably has lead-based paint, and houses from 1960 to 1990 may have it on the exterior. A lab test of paint chips, or a contractor with x-ray detection equipment, can confirm it. Until then, avoid dry sanding and heat guns.

**Q: Do you paint commercial buildings?**
A: Yes. We paint storefronts, trim and exterior walls on commercial properties, and work can be scheduled after hours or on weekends to stay clear of customers and staff. Longer jobs come with a weekly progress update, so you know which side of the building is next.

**Q: How much does exterior painting cost?**
A: It depends on the size of the building, the surfaces, how much scraping and repair the walls need, access to high areas, and the paint. The on-site visit and written quote are free, and the quote lists the preparation, repairs and coats so you can see what you are paying for.

### Masonry & stucco
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/masonry-stucco

**Q: Why is my stucco cracking?**
A: Fine hairline cracks are common as stucco ages and the building moves with the seasons. Wider or growing cracks, or stucco that bulges or sounds hollow, usually point to water behind it or movement underneath. We find out which before patching, because a patch over an active problem won’t last.

**Q: Can you match my existing stucco texture?**
A: A close match is usually possible; a perfect one is rare. Texture depends on the mix and how it was applied, and old stucco has weathered, so a fresh patch can look different at first. On a large repair, a new finish coat over the whole wall gives the most even result.

**Q: What is repointing, and when is it needed?**
A: Repointing means raking out worn mortar between bricks or stones and packing in new mortar. It is due when joints are crumbling, recessed or cracked, or when water is getting into the wall. On older brick, the new mortar should be weaker than the brick, or the brick takes the damage.

**Q: Is a crack in my foundation a masonry repair?**
A: Not always. A foundation crack that is widening, leaking or offset is a structural question, and the City of Winnipeg requires a building permit for structural foundation repairs. Get a structural engineer’s assessment first; once that repair is settled, we can handle finishing work around it, such as stucco above grade.

**Q: Can masonry or stucco work be done in winter?**
A: Mostly it waits for warmer weather. Mortar and stucco need protection from freezing while they cure, so winter work means enclosing and heating the area, which adds cost. Otherwise, book the on-site visit in winter and the work for early in the season.

**Q: How much does stucco or masonry repair cost?**
A: It depends on the size of the damage, what caused it, access to the wall, and how much finishing the repair needs to blend in. The on-site visit and written quote are free, and the quote spells out what gets removed and rebuilt.

### Flooring
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/flooring

**Q: Can new flooring go over my existing floor?**
A: Sometimes. A floating floor can often go over sound, flat flooring, but layering raises the floor height at doors and transitions and can hide problems underneath. Tile, glue-down and soft or uneven floors usually need to come up. We check at the on-site visit and tell you which approach your rooms need.

**Q: What flooring suits a Winnipeg basement?**
A: Pick a product rated for below-grade concrete, such as luxury vinyl plank or tile, and plan moisture control under it. Solid hardwood is a poor fit for a basement slab. Test the slab for moisture before you choose, and fix any water problem first, because no flooring survives a wet basement.

**Q: How long does flooring installation take?**
A: It depends on the area, how much old flooring has to come up, how much subfloor repair and levelling the rooms need, and whether the product has to acclimatize first. Removal and prep can take as long as laying the new floor. Ask us at the on-site visit about the schedule for your rooms.

**Q: Should I worry about asbestos in old floor tiles?**
A: If the tiles or adhesive went down before 1990, test before removing them. Health Canada lists older floor tiles among materials that may contain asbestos, and the risk comes from disturbing them. Manitoba’s workplace rules treat suspect material as asbestos until testing shows otherwise, and asbestos has to be removed before other work disturbs it.

**Q: How much does flooring installation cost?**
A: Price depends on the area, the flooring you choose, how much old flooring has to come up, and how much subfloor repair or levelling the rooms need. The on-site visit and written quote are free, and the quote separates removal, preparation and installation so you can compare it with others.

### Demolition
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/demolition

**Q: Do you demolish whole buildings?**
A: No. We do interior and selective demolition ahead of a renovation. In Winnipeg, demolishing a building or part of one needs a demolition permit, and the City requires the applicant to hold a demolition contractor licence. For a whole building, hire a licensed demolition contractor.

**Q: Can you remove a wall to open up my kitchen?**
A: Yes, as part of a renovation. A non-structural partition can come out with the rest of the demolition. A load-bearing wall needs a beam and a building permit, so it is planned with the renovation rather than treated as stand-alone demolition. We tell you at the on-site visit which kind of wall you have.

**Q: What happens if asbestos is found?**
A: Work in that area stops until it is dealt with. Manitoba’s rules require asbestos that will be disturbed to be removed before demolition or alteration starts, and that removal is specialist work. Testing older materials before the strip-out is scheduled avoids a stop in the middle of the job.

**Q: How do you keep dust out of the rest of the building?**
A: The work area is sealed off with plastic barriers, floors and paths to the door are covered, and debris goes out by the shortest route. In occupied homes and businesses that stay open, the messiest work is planned for the times that disturb you least.

**Q: Can you strip out a commercial space while we stay open?**
A: Often, yes. Strip-outs can be scheduled after hours or on weekends, with the work area sealed off from the rest of the space and debris taken out on an agreed route. On longer jobs you get a progress update every week, so you know what is coming next.

**Q: How much does interior demolition cost?**
A: It depends on how much is coming out, how it was built, access for hauling debris, and whether older materials need testing. The on-site visit and written quote are free. When demolition is the first stage of a larger renovation with us, it is part of that project’s quote.

### Home Renovation Costs in Winnipeg (2026)
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/renovation-cost-winnipeg

**Q: How long does a renovation take in Winnipeg?**
A: It depends on the room. On our jobs, a typical bathroom takes two to three weeks, a kitchen four to six weeks once the cabinets are on site, and a basement four to eight weeks. Whole-home renovations usually run eight to sixteen weeks, and many straightforward additions take about the same once permits and materials are ready.

**Q: Do I need a permit to renovate in Winnipeg?**
A: Often, yes. Finishing a basement or creating a new bedroom requires a building permit, and the City of Winnipeg says kitchens and bathrooms may need one. Electrical and plumbing work need their own permits. Cosmetic work, such as painting or new flooring, doesn’t. We coordinate permits and inspections with the City or your local municipality.

**Q: How is the instant estimate different from a written quote?**
A: The instant estimator gives a starting range from the size and options you choose. It can’t see your house, so wiring, plumbing, structure and site conditions aren’t in it. The written quote comes after a free on-site visit, is based on measurements and the scope we agree, and is the final price.

**Q: What does a written renovation quote include?**
A: Ours sets out the scope of work and what is included, the permits and inspections the job needs, and the price, with taxes shown, so you know where you stand before work begins. When comparing quotes from different contractors, check them line by line: a lower total sometimes means something has been left out.

**Q: How do I get an exact price for my renovation?**
A: Book a free on-site visit, or call 431-866-5644, Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. We look at the space, talk through what you want, and follow up with a free written quote. If you want a ballpark first, the instant estimator gives you a starting range. We reply to every request within one business day.

### Basement Renovation Cost in Winnipeg (2026)
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/basement-renovations/cost

**Q: How long does a basement development take?**
A: Four to eight weeks for a typical basement. The order matters: any water problems first, then framing, insulation, electrical and plumbing, inspections before the walls are covered, then drywall and finishes. A bathroom, or a bedroom that needs an egress window, adds steps, and we plan them into the schedule from the start.

**Q: Do I need a permit to finish a basement in Winnipeg?**
A: Yes, if you are adding rooms, bedrooms or living space. The City of Winnipeg requires a building permit for basement development, plus separate electrical and plumbing permits, and wiring and plumbing are inspected before they are covered. Painting and flooring alone don’t need a building permit. We coordinate permits and inspections as part of the job.

**Q: Will my written quote match the estimator range?**
A: Not necessarily. The estimator gives a starting range from the size of your basement and the options you pick. The written quote comes after a free on-site visit, where we check moisture, ceiling height, the windows and where the mechanical sits, and agree the scope. That written quote, with taxes shown, is the final price.

**Q: What is included in a basement development quote?**
A: The scope we agree at the visit. A full basement typically covers moisture checks and prep, framing and insulation, electrical and heat runs, any egress window, bathroom or wet bar, then flooring, doors, trim and paint. Your written quote lists exactly what is in, including the permits and inspections the job needs.

**Q: How do I get an exact price for my basement?**
A: Book a free on-site visit, or call 431-866-5644, Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. We look at the space, ask how you want to use it, check what the windows and ceiling height allow, then send a free written quote. We reply to every request within one business day.

### Bathroom Renovation Cost in Winnipeg (2026)
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/bathroom-renovations/cost

**Q: How long does a bathroom renovation take?**
A: Two to three weeks for a typical full bathroom, from demolition to the final bead of silicone. If it’s your only bathroom, tell us at the on-site visit: we plan those tighter and get the toilet back in service as early as we can. During the work, we protect the hallway, seal off the room and clean up every day.

**Q: Do I need a permit to renovate a bathroom in Winnipeg?**
A: Often. The City of Winnipeg lists bathrooms among renovations that may need a building permit, and altering the plumbing system needs a plumbing permit. Replacing a faucet or fixture in the same spot, without changing the plumbing, doesn’t. We coordinate permits and inspections with the City or your local municipality as part of the job.

**Q: How is the estimator range different from my written quote?**

The written quote follows a free on-site visit, where we measure, look at the plumbing you already have and check the floor, and agree the scope with you. That written quote, with taxes shown, is the final price.

**Q: What is included in a bathroom renovation quote?**
A: One written price covering labour, materials and haul-away for the scope we agree. A full bathroom typically covers demolition, plumbing and electrical, backer board and waterproofing, tile, vanity and fixtures, then paint and finishing. If you want to swap a tile or a vanity later, we re-price it before anything is ordered.

**Q: How do I get an exact price for my bathroom?**

Cabinets and counters are ordered after you approve the written quote, and the countertop template happens after the cabinets are set, which adds about a week in the middle. We set up a temporary spot for your kettle and microwave while the work is on.

**Q: Do I need a permit for a kitchen renovation in Winnipeg?**

Cosmetic work, such as painting or new flooring, doesn’t need a building permit. We coordinate permits and inspections with the City or your local municipality as part of the job.

**Q: Is the estimator price the same as a quote?**

The written quote follows a free on-site visit, where we measure, look at the walls, plumbing and wiring, and agree the scope. That written quote, with taxes shown, is the final price.

## Quick answers

### How Much Does a Home Renovation Cost in Canada?
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-cost-canada
There’s no current official average for what a home renovation costs in Canada. Statistics Canada tracks how prices change instead, with price indexes for renovations and for new buildings; new residential building prices rose 2.3% in the year to the second quarter of 2026. In Winnipeg, our instant estimator starts bathrooms at $16,000, basements at $25,000 and kitchens at $40,000.

### Basement Development Permits in Winnipeg: How to Apply
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/basement-development-permits-winnipeg
In Winnipeg, you need a building permit to develop a basement when you add rooms, bedrooms or living space; painting, flooring and millwork alone don’t need one. Electrical and plumbing work need separate permits. A development permit may also apply, for example when added cooking equipment means the space may count as a secondary suite.

### Basement Flooding in Winnipeg: Backwater Valves, Sump Pits and Permits
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/basement-flood-protection-winnipeg
Most Winnipeg basement flooding comes from sewer backup or groundwater. A backwater valve stops sewage backing up through the floor drain; a sump pit collects weeping-tile water and pumps it outside. Homes built after 1979 were required to have a backwater valve, and homes built since 1990 a sump pit. The City’s old subsidy for both was cancelled.

### Clay Soil and Basement Cracks in Winnipeg: What’s Normal
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/clay-soil-basement-cracks-winnipeg
Winnipeg’s clay soil swells when it gets wet and shrinks as it dries, so foundations and basement floors move with the seasons. Fine, dry cracks are common, but a crack that is horizontal, widening, offset or leaking, or a wall that bows, should be assessed by a structural engineer before you finish the basement. Structural foundation repairs need a permit.

### Clinic Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What to Plan For
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/clinic-renovation-permits-winnipeg
Most clinic renovations in Winnipeg need a commercial building permit, applied for with the City's Commercial Alteration Design Summary, and many need a building occupancy permit before patients return. Clinics add their own steps: an electrical declaration for patient care areas, provincial approval and a shielding specification for X-ray rooms, and accessible design under the Manitoba Building Code.

### How Much Should an Ensuite Renovation Cost in Winnipeg?
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/ensuite-renovation-winnipeg
Priced like any bathroom of the same size and finish, an ensuite starts in our instant estimator at $16,000–$20,000 for up to 50 sq ft, $20,000–$24,000 for 51–100 sq ft and $24,000–$36,000 for 101–150+ sq ft; a new shower runs $10,000–$15,000. Plumbing moves, the shower, tile, glass and any enlargement decide where yours lands; see our bathroom renovation cost guide (https://bridgelandbuilders.com/services/bathroom-renovations/cost).

### When to Paint Your House Exterior in Winnipeg
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/exterior-painting-winnipeg-when-to-paint
In Winnipeg, exterior painting is done between late spring and early fall, when days and nights stay warm enough for the paint and surfaces are dry. The exact limits are on the product label: follow its minimum temperature and drying times, avoid painting before rain or heavy dew, and allow more time for preparation than for painting.

### Home Addition Zoning in Winnipeg: Permits and Variances
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-additions-and-zoning-winnipeg
Every house addition in Winnipeg needs a development permit under the Winnipeg Zoning By-law and a building permit under the Winnipeg Building By-law. Zoning controls where the addition sits and how big it can be; if a design does not fit, a variance may be possible. The 2025 zoning changes mainly affect two- to four-unit homes.

### Home Renovation Financing in Canada: Your Options
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-financing-canada
Most Canadians finance a renovation with savings, a home equity line of credit (up to 65% of the home's value), a refinance or home equity loan (generally up to 80%, including the existing mortgage), a personal loan or line of credit, or, for a new suite, CMHC-insured refinancing. The federal Greener Homes Loan is closed.

### Home Renovation Planning in Canada: Guide and Checklist
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/home-renovation-planning-guide-canada
Plan a renovation in this order: write down goals and must-haves, set a budget with a contingency, check which permits your municipality requires, get written quotes for the same scope, build a timeline around ordering and inspections, and test for asbestos and radon where relevant before demolition. Deciding early is what keeps the work on schedule.

### How to Check a Contractor's WCB Clearance in Manitoba
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba
Go to WCB Manitoba's website, open the Clearances page and choose the public Clearance Request System. Search by the contractor's business name or seven-digit WCB account number, tick the business, add it to your list, then click Request Letter and Submit. Print or save the letter. You don't need an account or registration.

### Insulation Rebates in Manitoba: How to Use Them During a Renovation
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/insulation-rebates-during-a-renovation-manitoba
Yes, you can claim Efficiency Manitoba's Home Insulation Rebate during a renovation, but only if it is approved before you buy materials or remove drywall, stucco or old insulation. A registered contractor or retailer starts the application, the rebate is paid per R-value added per square foot, and the insulation must be installed within 12 months of approval.

### Home Renovation Grants and Tax Credits in Manitoba
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/manitoba-renovation-tax-credits-rebates
Manitoba homeowners can still use two federal tax credits, the Multigenerational Home Renovation and Home Accessibility credits, Efficiency Manitoba rebates for insulation, windows and doors, Manitoba Hydro's on-bill Home Energy Efficiency Loan, and CMHC-insured refinancing to build a suite. The Greener Homes grant and loan and the City of Winnipeg's flood-protection subsidy are closed.

### Office Fit-Up in Winnipeg: Planning Around Your Lease
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/office-fit-up-lease-planning-winnipeg
Plan an office fit-up backwards from your lease. Before signing, get the landlord's consent to your plans, and settle what the landlord will build or pay for and who owns the improvements when you leave. Then allow time for drawings, a City building permit, inspections and an occupancy permit before your team moves in.

### Planning a Winter Basement Development in Winnipeg
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/planning-a-winter-basement-development-winnipeg
A Winnipeg winter is a practical time to develop a basement: the work is indoors, so it can carry on through the cold months. Plan the layout and permits in fall, run a radon test over the winter, sort out any egress window early, and expect 4–8 weeks of construction for a typical basement.

### Radon Testing Before Finishing a Basement in Manitoba
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/radon-testing-before-finishing-a-basement
Test before you finish. Health Canada recommends a long-term radon test of at least three months, ideally in fall or winter, and action if the result is above 200 Bq/m³. The usual fix, active soil depressurization by a C-NRPP certified professional, is easier to plan before walls and ceilings close in. Retest after the renovation.

### Heritage District Renovations: Updating a Character Home in Winnipeg
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/renovating-a-character-home-in-winnipeg
Most character homes in Winnipeg need only the usual building permits. Heritage rules apply when a house is on the City's List of Historical Resources or inside one of its two heritage conservation districts, Armstrong's Point and Crescentwood–Enderton Park. There, a heritage permit is needed before work that the listing or the district plan covers.

### Restaurant Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What You Need
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/restaurant-renovation-permits-winnipeg
A restaurant renovation in Winnipeg usually needs a City building permit, trade permits for electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, and a building occupancy permit before reopening. Before any construction, a Manitoba public health inspector reviews your floor plan, equipment and menu, and licensed premises must tell the Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority about major renovations.

### Secondary Suite Rules in Winnipeg: What the City Requires
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/secondary-suite-rules-winnipeg
Winnipeg allows one secondary suite per single-family property. It needs a development permit and a building permit before construction, plus electrical and plumbing permits. The City lists an attached suite’s size as no more than 33% of the combined floor area or 74 m² (800 sq. ft.), whichever is less, and at least 32.5 m² (350 sq. ft.).

### Spring Flood Prep for Winnipeg Basements: A Homeowner Checklist
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/spring-flood-prep-winnipeg-basements
Before the spring melt, clear snow away from your foundation and window wells, make sure eavestroughs and downspouts drain away from the house, test the sump pump by pouring water into the pit, check and clean the backwater valve, and lift appliances and belongings off the basement floor. Watch the Province’s flood outlooks and report flooding to 311.

### What Does a General Contractor Do?
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/what-does-a-general-contractor-do
A general contractor takes responsibility for delivering the whole project: pricing it, hiring and scheduling the trades, ordering materials, arranging permits and inspections, keeping the site safe, and handing over finished work. Instead of managing an electrician, plumber, framer and finisher separately, you sign one contract and deal with one point of contact.

### Window and Door Replacement in Winnipeg: Permits, Glass and Rebates
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/window-and-door-replacement-winnipeg
In Winnipeg, replacing windows and doors with the same size does not need a building permit, although building code and zoning rules still apply. New or larger openings may need one. Efficiency Manitoba pays $100 for each ENERGY STAR certified triple-pane window or door that replaces an existing unit; install first, then apply within 90 days.

### Renovation Permits in Winnipeg: What Needs One and How to Apply
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/winnipeg-renovation-permits
In Winnipeg, a building permit is usually needed when a renovation changes layout or structure: kitchens, bathrooms, new bedrooms, open-concept work, new or larger exterior openings, basements, additions and secondary suites. Cosmetic work such as painting, flooring and millwork doesn’t need one. Electrical and plumbing work need their own permits, and some projects also need a development permit.

### Winnipeg Renovation Show: Questions to Ask Contractors
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/winnipeg-renovation-show-questions-to-ask
The 2027 Winnipeg Renovation Show runs January 15 to 17 at the RBC Convention Centre. Bring photos, rough measurements and a budget range, ask every contractor the same questions about scope, permits, WCB coverage, insurance, schedule, payments and warranty, and don't sign anything until you have written quotes to compare.

### Commercial Interior Design: Balancing Function and Looks
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-balance-functionality-and-aesthetics-in-a-commercial-space
Decide how the space has to work first, then make it look like your brand within those limits. Settle exits, accessible routes, washrooms, plumbing, ventilation and lighting before choosing finishes, because they are costly to move later. Then pick durable materials, a consistent colour palette and signage that helps customers find their way.

### Full vs Partial Renovation: How to Choose for Your Winnipeg Home
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-choose-between-a-full-renovation-and-partial-upgrades
Choose a full renovation when the wiring, plumbing, insulation or layout need work in several rooms, or when you want the whole house finished to one standard at once. Choose partial upgrades when those systems are sound and only one or two rooms hold you back. Many homes suit a phased plan that does the system work first.

### Commercial Renovation ROI: Which Upgrades Pay Back?
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/understanding-roi-which-commercial-renovations-bring-the-most-value
No renovation comes with a guaranteed return. The upgrades most likely to pay back are tied to a measurable result: more customers or seats served, fewer staff hours lost to a poor layout, lower energy and maintenance bills, or a space that is easier to lease or sell. Estimate each one against how long you will use the space.

### Commercial Renovation Financing in Manitoba: Your Options
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-finance-a-commercial-renovation-without-breaking-the-bank
Most Manitoba businesses combine several sources: cash, a term loan or line of credit from a bank, credit union or BDC, a tenant improvement allowance from the landlord if they lease, and equipment financing for big-ticket items. Small businesses can also ask lenders about the federal Canada Small Business Financing Program. Bridgeland Builders does not provide financing.

### How to Choose a Renovation Contractor in Winnipeg
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-contractor-for-your-renovation-project
Verify before you compare prices: a current WCB Manitoba clearance, a liability insurance certificate, a registered business name, recent reviews and references, and a written contract that names who pulls permits, sets the deposit and payment schedule, and puts every change in writing. Then compare detailed written quotes for the same scope.

### The Biggest Cost Factors in Commercial Renovation Projects
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/the-biggest-cost-factors-in-commercial-renovation-projects
The biggest cost drivers in a commercial renovation are usually behind the walls, not the finishes: mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection changes; code requirements triggered by a change of use; hidden conditions such as asbestos; after-hours or phased work; and scope changes once construction starts. Complete drawings and a contingency keep them in check.

### Commercial Renovation Planning in Winnipeg: A Business Guide
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/how-to-prepare-your-business-for-a-major-renovation
Start from the date you need the space back and work backwards: written scope and quote, drawings, permits, construction in phases or after hours, inspections and the occupancy permit. Tell staff and customers early, keep accessible routes open or announce when they are not, and plan restocking, training and reopening for after the City allows occupancy.

### Bathroom Renovation Ideas That Add Value in Winnipeg Homes
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/which-bathroom-remodel-upgrades-offer-the-best-return-on-investment-for-canadian-homeowners
The bathroom upgrades that add the most value protect the house and make the room easier to live with: proper waterproofing, an exhaust fan vented outdoors, good lighting, practical storage and durable, easy-to-clean finishes. Accessibility features such as wall backing for future grab bars add long-term value at low cost while the walls are open.

### Small Kitchen Renovation Ideas for Winnipeg Homes
https://bridgelandbuilders.com/blog/essential-design-strategies-for-small-kitchen-renovations
Good small kitchen renovation ideas start with the layout, not the finishes. Choose the layout your room can actually hold, whether galley, L-shaped, U-shaped or peninsula, then add storage that reaches the ceiling, lighting under the upper cabinets and appliances sized for the space. Spend first on what changes how the kitchen works.
